text.aura: You give off candlelight. Not the stadium spotlight, the soft glow that makes a small room feel intimate and safe. Jeong carries a warm, focused, slightly mysterious energy. People feel drawn closer to you, often without knowing why, and once they're near, they feel understood. You have the kind of presence that makes strangers confide in you at a party at 1am. Your glow is detailed and personal: a thoughtful look, a perfect question, the feeling that you're truly paying attention. The glow-up for you isn't becoming louder to compete with brighter people. It's trusting that your quiet flame is magnetic exactly as it is, and letting more people see it instead of saving it only for a few.
text.how-people-read-you: In the first ten seconds: gentle, thoughtful, a little reserved. Some people think you're shy. Others sense there's a lot going on behind your eyes and get curious. You often come across as kind, artistic and emotionally intelligent, the person who remembers small details and asks the right follow-up question. The misreading: people can think you're cold or uninterested when you're actually just warming up. Candles take a moment to catch. You may also hide your intensity, so people underestimate how passionate you are about the things you love. To be read more clearly, let your warmth arrive a little earlier. Offer a compliment, share an opinion with feeling, laugh openly. People will realize the flame was there all along.
text.colors: Your base colors are soft, glowing Fire: rose, dusty pink, berry, wine, plum and warm lilac. These colors feel intimate and romantic on you, like candlelight on silk. Wood feeds your Fire, so deep green and olive make a beautiful pairing, especially in velvet or knit. Warm neutrals like cream, latte and soft camel keep your look cozy and refined. Add small touches of gold to catch the light, a thin chain, small hoops, a ring. Avoid colors that feel too harsh or neon for you, like electric blue or acid yellow in large amounts. They can drown your subtle glow. Your colors should feel like the inside of a favorite café on a winter evening.
text.style: Style-wise, you're romantic and detailed. Delicate jewelry, soft knits, silk blouses, lace edges, pieces with small, interesting details that people only notice up close. That's the point, your style rewards attention, just like you do. Vintage pieces with stories suit you deeply. You also look stunning in candlelit textures: velvet, satin, cashmere. Keep silhouettes soft rather than sharp. The trap is being so subtle that your style disappears in a crowd. Add one focal point: a beautiful earring, a deep lip, a meaningful necklace. Hair soft and touchable, makeup glowing rather than dramatic. Your best photo is in warm, low light, close-up, with a small smile, looking like you know a secret.
text.vibe: The glow-up you're after is the warm mystery who lets people in. Think of the quiet second lead in a webtoon, the one readers end up loving most, because their depth is real. The shift for you is visibility. Share your passions, the books, the music, the strange niche hobby, with people who aren't already your closest friends. Speak first sometimes. Wear the bolder lipstick on an ordinary day. Your intensity is attractive when it's expressed, not hidden. Also lean into creativity. Writing, photography, cooking, anything that lets the flame make something. People are drawn to someone who glows from the inside, and you've always had that. Now let it be seen from across the room.
text.aura-dims: You lose your glow when you've been giving warmth to everyone and not keeping any for yourself. You might look tired, withdrawn, a little hidden behind oversized sweaters and a phone screen. You start overthinking every interaction and saying less. Your glow feels flickery, like a candle in a draft. The reset is creating a small, cozy world just for you. An evening with good tea, a lit candle, a book, no messages. A long, quiet walk with your favorite album. Writing down what's been weighing on you. Seeing one friend who makes you feel completely safe. Then return to the world in something soft and beautiful. Your flame doesn't need more fuel from others. It needs protection from the wind.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, your aura is candlelight. People feel safe and seen around you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also think you're shy. You're not shy. You're judging the lighting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Rose, wine, velvet, tiny gold? You look like a winter love song.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: So subtle nobody notices. Add one thing people can see from the doorway.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is letting the warmth arrive earlier.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Speak first once this week. The flame was never the problem. The hiding is.

spring.intro: Spring's Wood keeps a Jeong flame well fed, so your aura is a lantern glowing at dusk. You come across as warm, attentive and quietly magnetic, drawn in one at a time rather than all at once. Your style instinct is soft lighting: candle colors, delicate jewelry, romantic details. With so much fuel, you can overdo the mood and end up looking precious, like a perfume advert nobody can approach. Your glow-up is grounding through Earth, the element your Fire creates: oatmeal, caramel, soft brown, simple ceramic or wooden accessories. Add one glowing detail, a tiny gold pendant or a garnet-red ring. You look best like a lamp in a cozy room with the door open.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Jeong, lace, pearls and candlelight on a Monday? Add an oatmeal jumper. Be reachable.

summer.intro: Born when Fire is everywhere, a summer Jeong is a candle at midday, burning brightly among bigger lights. Your aura reads as intense and expressive, and you may feel pressure to compete with louder people in louder colors. Your glow-up is choosing intimacy over volume. Water and Earth temper doubled Fire, so wear deep navy, slate, stone and taupe, and let your flame appear in one precise place: a red bag, plum earrings, a single gold cuff. Fine textures suit you better than big prints, a crisp poplin over a busy graphic. A summer Jeong at its best is noticed by the people who matter, not everyone in the room, and that is real magnetism.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Jeong, slate linen and one plum earring. The right people will notice. That's the point.

autumn.intro: Autumn gives a Jeong flame Metal to work on, the element Fire controls, so your aura is the smith's flame: focused, skilled and quietly powerful. You come across as competent and refined, sometimes intimidatingly so. Your style already leans precise, with good tailoring and thoughtful jewelry, but it can look severe by Friday. Your glow-up is rekindling warmth. Wood feeds your Fire, so moss, olive and walnut tones bring life, and soft knits or suede give your edges a friendlier finish. Keep one metallic piece that looks handmade, hammered rather than mirror-polished. The autumn Jeong glow is a craftsperson's lamp, lighting something beautiful made slowly and with care.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Jeong, you look like you'd correct my grammar. Walnut suede says you'd buy me coffee first.

winter.intro: Winter Water presses on Fire, so a winter Jeong is a candle in a cold window, and your aura reads as cozy, loyal and slightly protective of itself. People feel comforted around you and may not realize how much effort that warmth takes. Your wardrobe tends to go dark to blend into the season, black wool on black wool. Let the flame be seen: that's the whole glow-up. Wood feeds Fire, so deep greens give your look support, and warm reds, burgundy and amber make the candle visible. A soft wool coat in a rich color, a glowing pendant or amber-toned accessories turn your quiet into presence. A window is lovelier when the light is on.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Jeong, a burgundy coat is your candle in the window. Let people see it's lit.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Jeong, you carry the glow of a lamp in a clay room: soft, warm and very comforting. People relax near you and tell you things. The risk is fading into the cozy background. Fire feeds Earth, so lots of oatmeal and taupe can absorb your light. Your glow-up is a brighter flame. Wood feeds Fire, so sage or deep green helps, and one warm jewel tone, garnet or amber, gives people something to notice. Candlelight looks best with a little contrast around it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Jeong, you're the candle, not the clay. Wear the garnet.

strength.strong: A strong Jeong Fire aura is a lamp turned up to full. With plenty of Fire and Wood, you come across as intense, magnetic and very particular about your look. Every detail is curated, and people can feel the effort behind it. The blind spot is control: outfits so composed that nobody dares to tease you, colors so moody they feel like a closed door. Let something be slightly undone. Mix one casual piece into your polish, trainers with the good coat. Add a soft neutral that lowers the temperature. Your glow is strongest when it invites people closer instead of keeping them at the threshold.
strength.weak: A weak Jeong Fire aura is a candle in a draft, flickering and easy to miss. With little Fire or Wood support, you have depth and warmth but may hide behind neutral, unremarkable clothes chosen so nobody looks twice. The blind spot is shrinking: deciding you are simply not the kind of person who wears color or statement pieces. Your glow-up is one warm light. A burgundy scarf, a garnet-toned ring, an amber knit. Wear it every day for a week and notice who leans in to talk. Small flames are made to be noticed close up.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon

missing_fire.speaker: bom

missing_fire.speaker: yeon

missing_earth.speaker: bom

missing_earth.speaker: yeon

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
